data_description.show_in_sidebar: The table stays reachable from this integration's page when hidden.
data_description.low_threshold: Devices at or below this level are marked Low (red) and counted in the shopping summary.
data_description.warn_threshold: Levels above Low and up to this value are yellow, higher is green. Must be above the Low level.

data_description.replacement_jump: A rise of at least this many percentage points suggests the battery was replaced, and asks you to confirm.

import_battery_notes.title: Import from Battery Notes
import_battery_notes.description:
Takes over what Battery Notes knows, once. Nothing is changed in Battery Notes, and running it again adds nothing twice.

Found {devices} device(s) in Battery Notes. Would add {new_entries} last-replaced date(s) and set {type_updates} battery type(s). {already} date(s) are already in the history, {not_tracked} device(s) are not tracked by Battery Log.

Battery types that are not in your list are skipped and mentioned in the entry note: {unknown_types}. Add them to the list first to import them.

data_description.import_types: Only for devices that have no type yet, and only for types that exist in your list.
data_description.import_dates: Adds one history entry per device with the note "Imported from Battery Notes". Battery Notes may hold the day you started tracking rather than a real replacement, so check the dates afterwards.

detect_history.title: Detect past replacements
detect_history.description:
Looks at the battery level history Home Assistant has kept and finds moments when a battery was most likely replaced (a lasting jump back to full). Run it once, ideally right after setting up.

Confident findings are added to the history with the note "Detected from battery history". Less certain ones wait in the panel with an Add button for you to decide. Devices that already have entries you made yourself are left alone, nothing is ever overwritten, and Home Assistant does not break if something fails: you get a report with the counts and the error.

data.add_first_seen: Add the first-seen date for devices without any entry

data_description.dry_run: Counts what would happen and stores nothing. The scan is not marked as done, so you can run it again.
data_description.add_confident: When off, every finding waits in the panel for you.
data_description.add_first_seen: The date the device first reported a level, noted as "First seen on the network".
